description: Python library that gets every result from search APIs that cap how many results one query returns (GitHub search 1,000, Algolia 1,000, Elasticsearch from/size 10,000) by splitting the search into filter windows that each fit under the cap.
rules: uncapped never makes requests: pass split() a count(filters) -> int function that returns the total number of results for those filters, then page through each Window's filters with your own client.
A dimension missing from the filters dict is unconstrained; only add that filter to the query when its key is present.
Range and DateRange bounds are inclusive. If the API's max parameter is exclusive, send hi + step.
Set step to the smallest difference the source can tell apart, such as timedelta(milliseconds=1) for millisecond timestamps.
Only split on fields where each item has exactly one value (number, date, id, category), never on tags or keyword search.
After iterating, check run.stats.capped_windows and run.stats.unaccounted, and do not silence UncappedWarning.
If the source reports that a count is only an estimate, return max(estimate, cap + 1) from count so uncapped splits further until counts are exact.
If the data changes during the run, pass a cap below the real limit, such as cap=950 for a 1,000 limit.
